claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied fields.
The untreated alloy has poor compressive strength and is susceptible to cracking.
A single-step isothermal aging treatment can induce secondary-phase precipitation in the alloy.
Aging at approximately 500–550 °C for 2–4 hours is an appropriate range for controlled precipitation.
The aging treatment will produce fine, ductile precipitates at grain boundaries.
The intergranular precipitates will improve grain-boundary binding.
The precipitates will act as crack deflectors that blunt or arrest crack propagation.
Crack deflection and improved grain-boundary binding will enhance compressive strength and mechanical integrity.
A nanoscale precipitate distribution will not impede the lattice instabilities or magnetostructural transformation responsible for the caloric response.
The aged alloy will achieve a compressive strength exceeding 152 MPa.
The caloric response of the aged alloy will remain within approximately ±10% of that of the untreated alloy.
The treatment will preserve caloric performance under magnetic-field or pressure-field operation near the phase-transformation temperature.
The proposed alloy and treatment remain rare-earth-free.
The mechanical benefit is expected under compressive loading rates comparable to those used in prior studies.
